At 1:30 p.m. Eastern, Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) and CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) were each up 21%, IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) was up 25%, TeraWulf (NASDAQ: WULF) was up 13% and Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) was up 12%. Leading ETFs showed software up closer to 4% and semiconductors up 13%. Bleeker also pointed to two company-specific items. The New York Times reported that Anthropic's demand is so large that SpaceX needs new data centers by October to fill its orders. On Friday, Oracle said it has secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. Bleeker notes Nvidia helped build neoclouds with funding, technical expertise and chips. He calls it a one-day win. Nebius is down 38% over the past month, CoreWeave 12% and Oracle 10%. Over six months Nebius is down more than 50%, Oracle 40% and CoreWeave 55%. Bleeker names three drivers of the selloff: higher rates and wider credit default swaps, political worries after the midterms, and Huang's removal. Only the last has reversed. Brian is joined by New Street Research technology infrastructure analyst Antoine Chkaiban on the new checks around Huang and why he's still a buyer; "In the Loop" host Ejaz on key-man risk and whether the "Bank of Nvidia" reopens for neoclouds; EMJ Capital founder and president Eric Jackson, who calls the return a win for open-source AI; Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman on the board's credibility and Colette Kress's future; Moor Insights & Strategy founder and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead on the politics behind the ouster and why nothing changes for AMD for 18 months; and SlateStone Wealth partner and chief market strategist Kenny Polcari on whether this kicks off a year-end rally.
